display.text:
# Deployment

## Project Site (GitHub Pages)

The static site in `website/` is published to
**[https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**
by [`.github/workflows/pages.yml`](../.github/workflows/pages.yml).

- A push to `main` runs the website tests, builds `_site` from `website/`, and
  deploys the artifact with `actions/deploy-pages`.
- `workflow_dispatch` republishes the site from the Actions tab without a code
  change.
- Pages is configured with the "GitHub Actions" source, so there is no
  `gh-pages` branch. Removing `pages.yml` stops all publishing and the site
  returns 404.
- The `github-pages` environment only allows deployments from `main`.

## Hosted MCP Server

The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**,
Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.

## Test Chat (UI)

Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:

> **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)**

## MCP Server Endpoint

Integrate via the MCP protocol at:

> **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach
> out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a
> client.

## Hosted Studio

The Living Studio SPA is deployed to Cloudflare Workers:

| Environment | URL |
|---|---|
| Production (`main`) | **[https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)** |
| Pull request preview | Posted automatically by Cloudflare Workers Builds as a PR comment |

Production deploys on every push to `main`. The Worker is `agentic-odi`; keep
`name` in `wrangler.jsonc` aligned with the Worker connected in the dashboard.
Preview builds run for non-production branches and are ephemeral: the Cloudflare
PR comment is the source of truth, so do not copy a preview URL into docs. The
hosted UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the
sidecar tunnel described below.

## Living Studio on a Free Cloudflare Worker

Workers Containers — the only way to run the Python sidecar entirely on
Cloudflare — requires the Workers Paid plan. On the free plan, the Worker serves
the built SPA as Workers Static Assets and proxies `/api/*` to the sidecar
through a free, account-less
[Cloudflare Quick Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/quick-tunnels/).

`wrangler.jsonc` publishes `apps/studio/dist` with SPA fallback and runs the Worker
first for `/api/*`; `infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` forwards those calls to the
`SIDECAR_URL` secret. The browser only talks to the Worker origin, so the
sidecar's CORS list is not involved.

Every response from the Worker — static assets and proxied API calls alike —
carries a content security policy (`default-src 'self'`, `connect-src 'self'`,
`frame-ancestors 'none'`) plus `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`,
`X-Frame-Options: DENY`, a strict referrer policy, and a Permissions Policy that
disables geolocation, camera, and microphone. `tests/test_worker_security_headers.py`
pins those headers so a preview deployment can be smoke-tested against them.

```bash
# 1. Build the SPA that the Worker uploads as static assets
npm --prefix apps/studio ci
npm --prefix apps/studio run build

# 2. Terminal A — MCP server (:8000) + sidecar (:8100)
python scripts/dev.py

# 3. Terminal B — free public URL for the sidecar (no account required)
cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8100
# copy the https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL it prints

# 4. Store the URL on the Worker, then deploy
npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL   # paste the trycloudflare URL
npx wrangler deploy
```

Workers Builds settings (Workers & Pages → your Worker → Settings → Builds):

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Production branch | `main` |
| Root directory | `/` |
| Build command | `npm --prefix apps/studio ci && npm --prefix apps/studio run build` |
| Deploy command | `npx wrangler deploy` |
| Preview command | `npx wrangler preview` |

A Worker has no run command: the Worker script runs on Cloudflare. Set `name` in
`wrangler.jsonc` to the Worker you created before the first deploy.

### Pull request previews

Workers Builds posts the build status and Preview URL to the pull request
automatically. To enable it:

1. Open the Worker → **Settings** → **Build** → **Branch control**.
2. Keep the production branch set to `main` and enable **Preview Builds**.
3. If Cloudflare shows **Set up Worker Previews**, complete the one-time switch.
   This cannot be reversed.
4. Confirm the Preview command is `npx wrangler preview`.

`wrangler.jsonc` must keep a `previews` block, even an empty one: the
`wrangler preview` command fails the build with "Your Wrangler configuration is
missing a `previews` block" without it. Assets and compatibility settings stay
at the top level, so `"previews": {}` is enough while Previews need no extra
settings. If a future Preview needs vars or bindings, add them under `previews`
with Preview-safe values.

Previews do not inherit production settings. The SPA loads from a Preview, but
`/api/*` returns `502 SIDECAR_URL is not configured` until a preview-specific
`SIDECAR_URL` secret is configured:

```bash
npx wrangler preview secret put SIDECAR_URL --name <branch>
```

When `--name` is omitted it defaults to the current git branch. Previews are
ephemeral, and pull requests from forks may not receive one. If Cloudflare does
not comment, paste the URL into the PR's **Deployment** section.

The `cf` CLI can inspect build triggers and recent builds (`cf builds triggers
list`, `cf builds list`) and create a Preview (`cf previews deploy`), but it does
not post GitHub PR comments. The Workers Builds Git integration owns the PR link;
`cf` is only an optional verification tool and requires `cf auth login`.

> [!NOTE]
> The sidecar runs on your machine, so the Worker only works while
> `python scripts/dev.py` and the Quick Tunnel are running. Quick Tunnel URLs
> change on every restart — update the secret with
> `npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL`. Chat also needs a reachable
> OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the Studio's **Settings**; the canvas, job map,
> and impact simulation work without one.

1: /**
2:  * Free-plan Living Studio Worker.
3:  *
4:  * Workers Static Assets serve the built SPA from `apps/studio/dist`. Requests under
5:  * `/api/*` are forwarded to the Python sidecar (`apps/studio-api`), which runs on
6:  * the developer's machine and is published by a free Cloudflare Quick Tunnel.
7:  * (Running the sidecar inside Cloudflare requires Workers Containers, which is
8:  * a paid-plan feature.)
9:  */
10: 
11: interface Env {
12:   ASSETS: Fetcher;
13:   /** Public origin of the sidecar, e.g. https://random.trycloudflare.com */
14:   SIDECAR_URL?: string;
15: }
16: 
17: const API_PREFIX = "/api/";
18: 
19: /**
20:  * Defense-in-depth headers on every Response, assets and API alike.
21:  *
22:  * The SPA loads only its own bundle, talks to the Worker origin at `/api/*`, and
23:  * uses React inline styles, hence `'unsafe-inline'` for styles but nothing for
24:  * scripts. `connect-src 'self'` keeps a compromised bundle from exfiltrating
25:  * to another origin; `frame-ancestors` repeats the `X-Frame-Options` intent for
26:  * browsers that only honor the CSP directive.
27:  */
28: const SECURITY_HEADERS: Record<string, string> = {
29:   "Content-Security-Policy": [
30:     "default-src 'self'",
31:     "script-src 'self'",
32:     "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
33:     "img-src 'self' data: blob:",
34:     "font-src 'self' data:",
35:     "connect-src 'self'",
36:     "object-src 'none'",
37:     "base-uri 'self'",
38:     "form-action 'self'",
39:     "frame-ancestors 'none'",
40:   ].join("; "),
41:   "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
42:   "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
43:   "Referrer-Policy": "strict-origin-when-cross-origin",
44:   "Permissions-Policy": "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()",
45: };
46: 
47: function secure(response: Response): Response {
48:   const headers = new Headers(response.headers);
49:   for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(SECURITY_HEADERS)) {
50:     headers.set(name, value);
51:   }
52:   // Reuse the body stream so SSE (`/api/chat`) keeps streaming.
53:   return new Response(response.body, {
54:     status: response.status,
55:     statusText: response.statusText,
56:     headers,
57:   });
58: }
59: 
60: function sidecarError(detail: string): Response {
61:   return Response.json({ detail }, { status: 502 });
62: }
63: 
64: export default {
65:   async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
66:     const url = new URL(request.url);
67: 
68:     if (!url.pathname.startsWith(API_PREFIX)) {
69:       return secure(await env.ASSETS.fetch(request));
70:     }
71: 
72:     const sidecar = env.SIDECAR_URL?.trim().replace(/\/+$/, "");
73:     if (!sidecar) {
74:       return secure(sidecarError("SIDECAR_URL is not configured"));
75:     }
76: 
77:     // The Quick Tunnel routes by hostname, so the Worker's Host must not leak.
78:     const headers = new Headers(request.headers);
79:     headers.delete("host");
80:     headers.delete("cf-connecting-ip");
81: 
82:     const target = new URL(`${url.pathname}${url.search}`, `${sidecar}/`);
83: 
84:     try {
85:       // Returning the upstream Response directly preserves SSE streaming for
86:       // `/api/chat`.
87:       return secure(
88:         await fetch(
89:           new Request(target, {
90:             method: request.method,
91:             headers,
92:             body: request.body,
93:             redirect: "manual",
94:           }),
95:         ),
96:       );
97:     } catch (error) {
98:       return secure(sidecarError(`Sidecar unreachable: ${(error as Error).message}`));
99:     }
100:   },
101: } satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

"""MCP hydration and passthrough writes, ported from the Streamlit app."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
from typing import Any

from agentic_odi_core import ODIService, ToolName
from agentic_odi_core.remote import (
    StudioError,
    StudioErrorCode,
    parse_tool_result,
    tool_result_text,
)
from fastmcp import Client as McpClient
from fastmcp.exceptions import ToolError

from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.errors import StudioHTTPError
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.probes import is_endpoint_reachable
from agentic_odi_studio_api.studio.seed import seed_payload

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT = 3.0


async def fetch_canvas(mcp_url: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Fetch live canvas data from FastMCP, falling back to the seed prototype."""
    jobs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    warnings: list[str] = []

    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        log.warning("MCP endpoint unreachable at %s — falling back to seed data", mcp_url)
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["MCP endpoint unreachable"]}

    try:
        mcp_client = McpClient(mcp_url)
        async with mcp_client:
            raw_jobs = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOBS.value, {}), timeout=1.5
            )
            try:
                parsed_jobs = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_jobs))
                if isinstance(parsed_jobs, list):
                    jobs = parsed_jobs
            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                log.warning("Failed to parse jobs from MCP: %s", exc)
                jobs = []

            for job in jobs:
                job_id = job.get("id")
                if not job_id:
                    continue

                try:
                    raw_steps = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_JOB_MAP.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_steps = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_steps))
                    if isinstance(parsed_steps, list):
                        steps.extend(parsed_steps)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch steps for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)

                try:
                    raw_outcomes = await asyncio.wait_for(
                        mcp_client.call_tool(ToolName.GET_OUTCOMES.value, {"job_id": job_id}),
                        timeout=1.0,
                    )
                    parsed_outcomes = json.loads(tool_result_text(raw_outcomes))
                    if isinstance(parsed_outcomes, list):
                        outcomes.extend(parsed_outcomes)
                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
                    msg = f"Failed to fetch outcomes for job {job_id}: {exc}"
                    log.warning(msg)
                    warnings.append(msg)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        log.warning("MCP canvas hydration failed entirely: %s", exc)
        warnings.append(f"MCP hydration error: {exc}")

    if not jobs:
        return {**seed_payload(), "source": "seed", "warnings": ["No jobs returned from MCP"]}

    return {
        "jobs": jobs,
        "steps": steps,
        "outcomes": outcomes,
        "source": "mcp",
        "warnings": warnings,
    }


def fetch_local_canvas(service: ODIService) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Read the canvas directly from the local service, no HTTP round trip."""
    jobs = [job.model_dump() for job in service.get_jobs()]
    steps: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    outcomes: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for job in jobs:
        job_id = job["id"]
        steps.extend(step.model_dump() for step in service.get_job_map(job_id))
        outcomes.extend(outcome.model_dump() for outcome in service.get_outcomes(job_id))
    return {"jobs": jobs, "steps": steps, "outcomes": outcomes, "source": "local"}


async def call_mcp_tool(mcp_url: str, tool: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Invoke an MCP tool, surfacing failures as typed HTTP errors."""
    if not is_endpoint_reachable(mcp_url, timeout=0.3):
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
                message=f"MCP server unreachable at {mcp_url}",
                retryable=True,
            )
        )

    try:
        async with McpClient(mcp_url) as mcp_client:
            result = await asyncio.wait_for(
                mcp_client.call_tool(tool, arguments), timeout=MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT
            )
    except StudioHTTPError:
        raise
    except ToolError as exc:
        # The tool ran and refused: that is the tool's failure, not the
        # server's, and it is not worth retrying.
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_TOOL_FAILED,
                message=f"The {tool} tool failed: {exc}",
                retryable=False,
            )
        ) from exc
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        raise StudioHTTPError(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,
                message=f"Error calling {tool}: {exc}",
                retryable=True,
            )
        ) from exc

    text = tool_result_text(result)
    problem = parse_tool_result(text)
    if problem is not None:
        raise StudioHTTPError(problem)
    return text

735:   const sendMessage = useCallback(
736:     async (text: string) => {
737:       const trimmed = text.trim();
738:       if (!trimmed || streaming) {
739:         return;
740:       }
741: 
742:       const history: ChatMessage[] = [...messages, { role: "user", content: trimmed }];
743:       const assistantIndex = history.length;
744:       setMessages([...history, { role: "assistant", content: "", parts: [] }]);
745:       setStreaming(true);
746:       setThinkingPhase("health_check");
747:       setOfflineReply(false);
748:       setToolActivity([]);
749: 
750:       const controller = new AbortController();
751:       abortRef.current = controller;
752: 
753:       let content = "";
754:       let parts: ChatPart[] = [];
755:       let failure: StudioError | null = null;
756:       let terminal = false;
757:       let stopped = false;
758: 
759:       // Prose is appended to the open text part; a surface opens a new one, so
760:       // the transcript keeps the agent's order instead of gathering all prose
761:       // above all cards.
762:       const appendText = (text: string) => {
763:         if (!text) {
764:           return;
765:         }
766:         content += text;
767:         const last = parts[parts.length - 1];
768:         parts =
769:           last?.kind === "text"
770:             ? [...parts.slice(0, -1), { kind: "text", text: last.text + text }]
771:             : [...parts, { kind: "text", text }];
772:       };
773: 
774:       const publish = () => {
775:         setMessages((prev) => {
776:           const next = [...prev];
777:           next[assistantIndex] = {
778:             role: "assistant",
779:             content,
780:             parts: [...parts],
781:             ...(failure ? { error: failure, retryText: trimmed } : {}),
782:           };
783:           return next;
784:         });
785:       };
786: 
787:       const handleEvent = (event: RawSseEvent) => {
788:         switch (event.event) {
789:           case "status": {
790:             const phase = String(event.data.phase ?? "");
791:             setThinkingPhase(phase);
792:             if (phase === "offline") {
793:               setOfflineReply(true);
794:             }
795:             break;
796:           }
797:           case "delta": {
798:             appendText(String(event.data.text ?? ""));
799:             publish();
800:             break;
801:           }
802:           case "ui": {
803:             // Validate again on arrival: the connection is local but the
804:             // renderer must never trust a shape it has not checked.
805:             const parsed = parseUiSpec(event.data.spec, catalogManifest());
806:             if (parsed.ok) {
807:               parts = [
808:                 ...parts,
809:                 { kind: "ui", id: String(event.data.id ?? `ui-${parts.length}`), node: parsed.node },
810:               ];
811:               publish();
812:             }
813:             break;
814:           }
815:           case "tool":
816:             setToolActivity((prev) => [
817:               ...prev,
818:               {
819:                 name: String(event.data.name ?? ""),
820:                 status: String(event.data.status ?? ""),
821:                 preview: event.data.preview ? String(event.data.preview) : undefined,
822:               },
823:             ]);
824:             break;
825:           case "message": {
826:             terminal = true;
827:             content = String(event.data.content ?? content);
828:             const hasSurfaces = parts.some((part) => part.kind === "ui");
829:             if (!hasSurfaces) {
830:               parts = content ? [{ kind: "text", text: content }] : [];
831:             }
832:             publish();
833:             break;
834:           }
835:           case "conversation": {
836:             const id = String(event.data.id ?? "");
837:             if (id) {
838:               setConversationId(id);
839:             }
840:             break;
841:           }
842:           case "memory": {
843:             const observation = event.data.observation as Observation | undefined;
844:             if (observation?.id) {
845:               setMemory((prev) =>
846:                 prev.some((item) => item.id === observation.id)
847:                   ? prev.map((item) => (item.id === observation.id ? observation : item))
848:                   : [...prev, observation],
849:               );
850:             }
851:             break;
852:           }
853:           case "canvas_dirty":
854:             void refreshCanvas();
855:             break;
856:           case "connector": {
857:             if (String(event.data.status ?? "") === "error") {
858:               const reason = String(event.data.error ?? "The connector could not be added.");
859:               setMessages((prev) => [
860:                 ...prev,
861:                 { role: "notice", content: `Connector failed: ${reason}` },
862:               ]);
863:             } else {
864:               setConnectorSuggestions((prev) => {
865:                 const id = String(event.data?.preset ?? event.data?.name ?? "");
866:                 if (!id || prev.includes(id)) {
867:                   return prev;
868:                 }
869:                 return [...prev, id];
870:               });
871:             }
872:             void refreshConnectors();
873:             break;
874:           }
875:           case "error": {
876:             terminal = true;
877:             failure = readStudioError(event.data.error);
878:             publish();
879:             break;
880:           }
881:           default:
882:             break;
883:         }
884:       };
885: 
886:       try {
887:         await streamChat(
888:           {
889:             base_url: settings.base_url,
890:             api_key: settings.api_key,
891:             model: settings.model_name,
892:             mcp_url: settings.mcp_url,
893:             messages: history,
894:             brief,
895:             ui_catalog: catalogManifest(),
896:             conversation_id: conversationId,
897:           },
898:           handleEvent,
899:           controller.signal,
900:         );
901:       } catch (error) {
902:         const aborted = (error as Error).name === "AbortError";
903:         if (aborted) {
904:           // An abort is the user's own doing: drop the empty placeholder, keep
905:           // the question, and report no failure — the assistant did not break.
906:           stopped = true;
907:           setMessages((prev) => {
908:             const next = [...prev];
909:             if (next.length && next[next.length - 1].role === "assistant" && !next[next.length - 1].content) {
910:               next.pop();
911:             }
912:             return next;
913:           });
914:         } else {
915:           terminal = true;
916:           failure = asStudioError(error);
917:           publish();
918:         }
919:       } finally {
920:         if (!terminal && !failure && !stopped) {
921:           // The stream ended without a message or an error: something failed
922:           // silently, and the user must still be told.
923:           failure = {
924:             code: "internal",
925:             message: "The assistant stopped before answering.",
926:             suggestion: "Try again — your question is still here.",
927:             retryable: true,
928:           };
929:           publish();
930:         }
931:         setStreaming(false);
932:         setThinkingPhase(null);
933:         abortRef.current = null;
934:       }
935:     },
936:     [
937:       messages,
938:       streaming,
939:       settings,
940:       brief,
941:       conversationId,
942:       refreshCanvas,
943:       refreshConnectors,
944:     ],
945:   );

1: /**
2:  * Feature flags for the studio client.
3:  *
4:  * A flag is resolved once per read, highest precedence first:
5:  *
6:  *   1. `?flags=<name>:<value>`      — QA and demos without a rebuild
7:  *   2. `localStorage["studio.flags.<name>"]`
8:  *   3. the flag's build-time env variable
9:  *   4. the flag's declared default
10:  *
11:  * Unknown values fall through to the next source, so a typo in a query string
12:  * can never silently change behaviour.
13:  */
14: 
15: export type FeatureFlagName = "firstRunWizard";
16: 
17: export interface FeatureFlagDefinition {
18:   name: FeatureFlagName;
19:   description: string;
20:   envVar: string;
21:   defaultEnabled: boolean;
22: }
23: 
24: export const FEATURE_FLAGS: Record<FeatureFlagName, FeatureFlagDefinition> = {
25:   firstRunWizard: {
26:     name: "firstRunWizard",
27:     description: "Four-step welcome tour for first-time Living Studio users.",
28:     envVar: "VITE_STUDIO_FIRST_RUN_WIZARD",
29:     defaultEnabled: true,
30:   },
31: };
32: 
33: export const FLAG_STORAGE_PREFIX = "studio.flags.";
34: export const FLAG_QUERY_PARAM = "flags";
35: 
36: export type FlagSource = "query" | "storage" | "env" | "default";
37: 
38: export interface ResolvedFlag {
39:   enabled: boolean;
40:   source: FlagSource;
41:   raw: string | null;
42: }
43: 
44: export interface FlagSources {
45:   env?: string | null;
46:   stored?: string | null;
47:   query?: string | null;
48: }
49: 
50: const TRUTHY = new Set(["1", "true", "on", "yes", "enabled"]);
51: const FALSY = new Set(["0", "false", "off", "no", "disabled"]);
52: 
53: export function parseFlagValue(raw: string | null | undefined): boolean | null {
54:   if (raw === null || raw === undefined) {
55:     return null;
56:   }
57:   const normalized = raw.trim().toLowerCase();
58:   if (TRUTHY.has(normalized)) {
59:     return true;
60:   }
61:   if (FALSY.has(normalized)) {
62:     return false;
63:   }
64:   return null;
65: }
66: 
67: function readEnvFlag(definition: FeatureFlagDefinition): string | null {
68:   const env = import.meta.env as Record<string, unknown>;
69:   const raw = env[definition.envVar];
70:   if (raw === undefined || raw === null) {
71:     return null;
72:   }
73:   return String(raw);
74: }
75: 
76: function readStoredFlag(definition: FeatureFlagDefinition): string | null {
77:   if (typeof window === "undefined") {
78:     return null;
79:   }
80:   try {
81:     return window.localStorage.getItem(`${FLAG_STORAGE_PREFIX}${definition.name}`);
82:   } catch {
83:     // Private browsing modes can deny storage access.
84:     return null;
85:   }
86: }
87: 
88: /** `?flags=firstRunWizard:off,otherFlag:on` */
89: function readQueryFlag(definition: FeatureFlagDefinition): string | null {
90:   if (typeof window === "undefined") {
91:     return null;
92:   }
93:   const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
94:   for (const group of params.getAll(FLAG_QUERY_PARAM)) {
95:     for (const pair of group.split(",")) {
96:       const separator = pair.indexOf(":");
97:       if (separator === -1) {
98:         continue;
99:       }
100:       if (pair.slice(0, separator).trim() !== definition.name) {
101:         continue;
102:       }
103:       const value = pair.slice(separator + 1).trim();
104:       if (value) {
105:         return value;
106:       }
107:     }
108:   }
109:   return null;
110: }
111: 
112: function defaultSources(definition: FeatureFlagDefinition): Required<FlagSources> {
113:   return {
114:     query: readQueryFlag(definition),
115:     stored: readStoredFlag(definition),
116:     env: readEnvFlag(definition),
117:   };
118: }
119: 
120: export function resolveFlag(name: FeatureFlagName, sources?: FlagSources): ResolvedFlag {
121:   const definition = FEATURE_FLAGS[name];
122:   const resolved = sources ?? defaultSources(definition);
123: 
124:   const candidates: { source: FlagSource; raw: string | null | undefined }[] = [
125:     { source: "query", raw: resolved.query },
126:     { source: "storage", raw: resolved.stored },
127:     { source: "env", raw: resolved.env },
128:   ];
129: 
130:   for (const candidate of candidates) {
131:     const parsed = parseFlagValue(candidate.raw);
132:     if (parsed !== null) {
133:       return { enabled: parsed, source: candidate.source, raw: candidate.raw ?? null };
134:     }
135:   }
136: 
137:   return { enabled: definition.defaultEnabled, source: "default", raw: null };
138: }
139: 
140: export function isFeatureEnabled(name: FeatureFlagName, sources?: FlagSources): boolean {
141:   return resolveFlag(name, sources).enabled;
142: }
143: 
144: /** Persist a local override. Pass `null` to fall back to env/default. */
145: export function setFeatureOverride(name: FeatureFlagName, enabled: boolean | null): void {
146:   if (typeof window === "undefined") {
147:     return;
148:   }
149:   const key = `${FLAG_STORAGE_PREFIX}${name}`;
150:   try {
151:     if (enabled === null) {
152:       window.localStorage.removeItem(key);
153:       return;
154:     }
155:     window.localStorage.setItem(key, enabled ? "on" : "off");
156:   } catch {
157:     // Storage is an optimisation; the flag still resolves from env/default.
158:   }
159: }
160: 
161: export function clearFeatureOverride(name: FeatureFlagName): void {
162:   setFeatureOverride(name, null);
163: }

"""Connection probing and LLM health checks, ported from the Streamlit app."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import os
import socket
from urllib.parse import urlparse

from openai import AsyncOpenAI

DEFAULT_BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8001/v1"
DEFAULT_API_KEY = "local"
DEFAULT_MODEL = "local-tools-model"
DEFAULT_MCP_URL = "http://localhost:8000/mcp"

OFFLINE_MESSAGE = "LLM server offline (Local Studio Mode enabled)"


def _load_profile_fallback() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Read llm_profile.json directly without importing cli package."""
    import json
    from pathlib import Path

    xdg = os.getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
    cfg_dir = Path(xdg) / "agentic-odi" if xdg else Path.home() / ".config" / "agentic-odi"
    profile_file = cfg_dir / "llm_profile.json"
    if not profile_file.exists():
        return {}
    try:
        with open(profile_file) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {}


def defaults() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Streamlit-compatible environment defaults (same variable names).

    Priority order: environment variable > persisted llm_profile.json > hardcoded constant.
    """
    profile = _load_profile_fallback()
    return {
        "base_url": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL")
        or profile.get("base_url")
        or DEFAULT_BASE_URL,
        "api_key": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY") or profile.get("api_key") or DEFAULT_API_KEY,
        "model_name": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL") or profile.get("model") or DEFAULT_MODEL,
        "mcp_url": os.getenv("AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL") or profile.get("mcp_url") or DEFAULT_MCP_URL,
    }


def is_endpoint_reachable(url: str, timeout: float = 0.3) -> bool:
    """Quick socket check to verify a port is open without hanging on HTTP reads."""
    try:
        parsed = urlparse(url)
        host = parsed.hostname or "localhost"
        port = parsed.port or (443 if parsed.scheme == "https" else 80)
        with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=timeout):
            return True
    except OSError:
        return False


def classify_llm_error(exc: Exception) -> tuple[str, str]:
    message = str(exc)
    lower = message.lower()
    connection_indicators = [
        "connection error",
        "connection aborted",
        "failed to establish a new connection",
        "timed out",
        "timeout",
        "connection refused",
    ]
    if any(indicator in lower for indicator in connection_indicators):
        return "connection_error", message
    return "error", message


async def check_llm_health(base_url: str, api_key: str, model_name: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Non-blocking LLM health probe with an instant socket pre-check."""
    if not is_endpoint_reachable(base_url, timeout=0.3):
        return False, OFFLINE_MESSAGE

    client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=api_key, timeout=1.2)
    try:
        await asyncio.wait_for(client.models.list(), timeout=1.2)
        return True, "LLM backend is reachable."
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        status, detail = classify_llm_error(exc)
        return False, f"{status}: {detail}"

Now let me understand the core models/service and chat tool loop to know what can be done in browser. Also check docs/living-studio for "local mode" and capability. The CTO guidance suggests full local-first SQLite via OPFS. But the user's actual ask: "ensure that it may also run directly in the browser, through a back-of-the-front-end type of implementation that supports graceful progressive capability disclosure in that it works without the sidecart, but gets access to enhanced capabilities with it."

So the core deliverable is a BFF layer in the browser (service worker? client-side "back-of-front-end") that emulates the sidecar API for core entity CRUD and canvas, using browser storage (IndexedDB or OPFS SQLite WASM), and routes to sidecar when available for enhanced capabilities (chat/LLM, connectors, MCP, memory, conversations). Graceful capability disclosure.

A "Backend-for-Frontend" typically is a server-side aggregation layer. Here they want a client-side BFF in the browser. They say "back-of-the-front-end type of implementation". So we build a data-access abstraction (repository/adapter) in the SPA that:
- Implements the same API contract (StudioDataSource).
- Local implementation: IndexedDB/OPFS-based OLTP for Jobs/Steps/Outcomes, memory maybe.
- Remote implementation: existing sidecar fetch calls.
- Capability detection: probe `/api/config` and `/api/capabilities`; compose.
- Graceful progressive capability disclosure: features not available locally are disabled/hidden or show "requires sidecar" with setup instructions.

Need to decide storage engine: OPFS SQLite WASM vs IndexedDB. CTO says SQLite via OPFS is the ideal. But bringing SQLite WASM (e.g., @sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm) adds dependency, COOP/COEP headers for SharedArrayBuffer maybe. Actually sqlite-wasm OPFS VFS needs SharedArrayBuffer? The OPFS sqlite3 WASM supports `opfs` VFS with Atomics? In Chrome it uses synchronous access handles (no COOP/COEP required in recent versions?) There are caveats. A simpler reliable approach for this experiment could be IndexedDB (via `idb` or raw) with the same repository interface. The CTO guidance explicitly recommends SQLite via OPFS to keep parity with Tauri native SQLite. But browser native TS service would need to replicate domain logic. Alternatively, run the Python core compiled to WASM via Pyodide — heavy but parity. Hmm.

Let's think about what a realistic plan is for this repo, given tests and constraints.

Current stack:
- Python core: models, service, repository, SQLite.
- FastAPI sidecar with API.
- React SPA calling /api.
- Cloudflare Worker proxies /api to sidecar.

Goal: hosted version without sidecar works. Options:

Option A: Browser-local "BFF" in TypeScript that reimplements ODIService + repository on IndexedDB, and capability-aware API client. Enhanced with sidecar (chat, connectors, MCP, embedding). This is the most practical. It duplicates domain logic (small: models, scoring, CRUD) in TS. Risk of drift; can mitigate with shared contract JSON/schema and contract tests comparing behavior to Python. Core is only ~2300 lines; ODI entities CRUD. But duplication is real.

Option B: Compile the Python core to WASM and run it in a Web Worker, with SQLite WASM + OPFS. This preserves parity and allows the same repo logic. But Pyodide in browser is big (~10MB) and complex, and SQLite Python bindings won't work in Pyodide. Not viable with existing code without working around sqlite3. Could use sql.js and custom repository. Still heavy.

Option C: Client-side BFF with a service worker that intercepts /api and serves local CRUD from IndexedDB. Plus enhanced remote. Service worker adds complexity but makes the rest of SPA unchanged. However, service workers don't work in Tauri or some contexts; and developer complexity. Better to introduce an explicit data-access layer in SPA, not SW.

Option D: Keep sidecar API contract and implement local adapter in SPA. The "BFF" is a client-side module (e.g., `src/bff/`) with capability detection and adapters. This is clean and testable.

Given the CTO's guidance, we should follow local-first as source of truth. Local persistence for ODI entities. Then when sidecar is present, use it for enhanced capabilities: LLM chat (requires server or direct browser LLM call), connectors, MCP, memory, conversation history. But can also sync/merge. However, current architecture has sidecar as source of truth; the plan should migrate to local-first in browser. The question is how far to go: full local-first with sync? The ask is "run directly in browser" and "works without sidecar, enhanced with it". Enterprise CTO guidance suggests three tiers. But for this task, we likely need Tier 0 (local app) + Tier 1 (sidecar-enhancement) and graceful disclosure, not full SaaS replication with E2EE. But the guidance says "back-of-the-front-end type implementation" - maybe they specifically want BFF pattern.

We need to ask clarifying questions per brainstorming. Key open questions:
- Scope: should browser-local data be the source of truth permanently, or fallback/cache? Sync between local and sidecar? Or just use sidecar when available and local otherwise (with conflict resolution)?
- Storage engine: OPFS SQLite vs IndexedDB. Given CTO guidance, maybe use wa-sqlite/OPFS. But time/complexity. Need their preference.
- Which capabilities are must-have offline? CRUD + canvas + manual capture + scoring? Chat with direct LLM from browser (user's own endpoint) could work if CORS allows, but sidecar currently proxies to avoid CORS/API-key exposure. We could support direct LLM optionally? The guidance says enhanced with sidecar; chat likely sidecar-only initially. But maybe "enhanced capabilities" includes LLM, connectors, MCP.
- Deployment: Cloudflare Worker static SPA should work standalone; no SIDECAR_URL needed. Should we deploy a shared demo backend? Not asked.
- Backwards compatibility: sidecar API contract unchanged? Yes likely.
- Phases/milestones and tests/docs.

I should explore more to ground specifics:
- Core models/service: what exact operations need local implementation.
- Chat: what tools modify data; if chat requires sidecar, local canvas mutations from chat won't work offline. Fine.
- Memory: local-first? It's sidecar-local now. In browser, memory could use local storage/IndexedDB. But chat is enhanced capability; memory is useful only with chat. Could keep sidecar-only, or make local memory for local mode. The task says graceful progressive capability disclosure. We can treat memory/conversations as enhanced.
- Connectors: sidecar-only.
- UI: components rely on StudioContext and expect all fields. Need capability model to disable controls.

Let's read core services/models and chat loop perhaps. Also check tests for API/contract. And docs/living-studio.

"""Core domain models for Agentic ODI."""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field


class Direction(str, Enum):
    MINIMIZE = "minimize"
    MAXIMIZE = "maximize"


class BusinessImpactCategory(str, Enum):
    REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
    COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
    RETENTION = "retention"
    RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
    OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
    COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
    BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
    OTHER = "other"


def compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
    """ODI Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)."""
    return float(importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0.0))


class Job(BaseModel):
    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the Job-to-be-Done")
    description: str | None = Field(None, description="Detailed description of the Job")

from __future__ import annotations

10. Be warm, direct, and specific. Short sentences. No corporate jargon, no therapy-speak, no emojis."""


def _brief_lines(brief: StudioBrief | None) -> list[str]:
    if brief is None:
        return []
    facts = [
        ("Product", brief.product_name),
        ("Product URL", brief.product_url),
        ("Who it serves", brief.target_user),
        ("Job to be done", brief.job_statement),
        ("Core problem", brief.core_problem),
    ]
    return [f"- {label}: {value}" for label, value in facts if value.strip()]


def _brief_block(brief: StudioBrief | None) -> str:
    lines = _brief_lines(brief)
    if not lines:

        "\n\nThe user set this context during onboarding. Treat it as given and do not "
        "re-ask for it:\n" + "\n".join(lines)
    )


def offline_fallback(user_input: str, brief: StudioBrief | None = None) -> str:
    """Deterministic, honest guidance when no LLM backend is reachable.

    No fabricated customer data, no invented scores: the studio says what it can
    do by hand and points at the surface that does it.
    """
    lower_inp = user_input.lower()

    if brief is not None and brief.job_statement.strip():
        context = (
            f"\n\n**Working job:** {brief.job_statement.strip()}"
            if not brief.product_name.strip()
            else f"\n\n**{brief.product_name.strip()}** — {brief.job_statement.strip()}"
        )

        return (
            "### ODI, stage by stage\n\n"
            "1. **Define the job** — the functional progress a person is trying to make.\n"
            "2. **Capture desired outcomes** — `[direction] + [unit of measure] + [object of control] + [context]`.\n"
            "3. **Score the opportunity** — `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`; above 10 is underserved.\n"
            "4. **Map the job** — Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Conclude.\n\n"
            "Type `/capture` to record an outcome, `/jobmap` to walk the phases, "
            "and `/landscape` to see what is underserved." + context
        )

        return (
            "### Simulate the bet by hand\n\n"
            "Open **`/impact`** and pick the outcome you want to test. The simulation "
            "shows before/after friction; it no longer invents a result when no model "
            "is connected." + context
        )
    if "evidence" in lower_inp or "call" in lower_inp or "quote" in lower_inp:
        return (
            "### Evidence needs a source\n\n"
            "No connector is wired up, so there is no live transcript to quote. "

        "- `/landscape` — review what is underserved\n\n"

class _TurnFailure(Exception):

@@ -0,0 +1,612 @@
+# Local-First Storage with Optional Cloudflare D1 Sync Implementation Plan
+
+> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
+
+**Goal:** Add a sync-ready event store seam so local runs stay on SQLite, hosted runs use Cloudflare D1, and users can opt into authenticated sync or portable export/import.
+
+**Architecture:** `ODIService` is unchanged. `IntentStore` grows the sync fields and implements an `EventStore` protocol. `EventSourcedRepository` can sit over SQLite or D1. A new `agentic_odi_cloud` package provides the D1 REST provider, authenticated sync client, and JSONL bundles. A Worker owns D1 and Better Auth; local clients talk only to the sync API.
+
+**Tech Stack:** Python 3.10+, `httpx`, Cloudflare Workers, D1, Better Auth 1.5, TypeScript, Vitest, Miniflare.
+
+**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-storage-provider-sync-design.md`
+
+## Global Constraints
+
+- Python >= 3.10.
+- `packages/core` must continue to depend on no other workspace package.
+- Local mode must make zero data network calls.
+- `AGENTIC_ODI_STORAGE=local` always wins over D1 credentials.
+- Default local database remains `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`.
+- Tests run without Cloudflare credentials or network.
+- No secrets in source; `.dev.vars` is ignored.
+- Keep README/docs current in the same change.
+
+## Review Focus
+
+1. Malformed or hostile sync payloads must not corrupt local data or leak
+   another workspace's server sequence.
+2. Concurrent edits from two devices must converge to server order; deletes
+   must not be resurrected.
+3. Legacy databases must upgrade in place with unique event IDs and no loss.
+4. Local mode with D1 credentials present must still make no data network calls.
+5. Clock skew must not affect ordering; server sequence is authoritative.
+
+---
+
+### Task 1: Core event contract and SQLite migration
+
+**Files:**
+- Create: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/events.py`
+- Modify: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/intent_store.py`
+- Test: `packages/core/tests/test_events.py`
+- Test: `packages/core/tests/test_intent_store.py`
+
+**Interfaces:**
+- Produces: `Event`, `EventStore`, `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE`, `DEFAULT_DEVICE`,
+  `new_event_id()`, `resolve_device_id(path: Path | None = None) -> str`.
+- Produces: `IntentStore.append(...) -> Event`, `get_stream(...) -> list[Event]`,
+  `insert_remote(events) -> int`, `mark_synced(mapping) -> int`,
+  `retag_workspace(old, new) -> int`, `max_server_seq(workspace_id) -> int`,
+  `get_cursor(workspace_id) -> int`, `set_cursor(workspace_id, url, seq)`,
+  `pending_count(workspace_id) -> int`, `clear(workspace_id=None)`.
+
+- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing tests**
+
+```python
+def test_legacy_db_backfills_unique_event_ids(tmp_path):
+    db = tmp_path / "odi.db"
+    conn = sqlite3.connect(db)
+    conn.execute("CREATE TABLE events (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, timestamp TEXT NOT NULL, event_type TEXT NOT NULL, payload TEXT NOT NULL)")
+    conn.execute("INSERT INTO events (timestamp, event_type, payload) VALUES ('2026-01-01T00:00:00', 'JOB_CREATED', '{\"id\": \"j1\"}')")
+    conn.commit(); conn.close()
+
+    store = IntentStore(str(db))
+    events = store.get_stream()
+    assert len(events) == 1
+    assert events[0]["event_id"]
+    assert events[0]["workspace_id"] == "local"
+    assert events[0]["device_id"] == "local"
+    assert events[0]["server_seq"] is None
+```
+
+```python
+def test_append_returns_event_and_duplicate_event_id_is_idempotent(tmp_path):
+    store = IntentStore(str(tmp_path / "e.db"))
+    first = store.append("JOB_CREATED", {"id": "j1"}, event_id="evt-1")
+    second = store.append("JOB_CREATED", {"id": "j1"}, event_id="evt-1")
+    assert first["event_id"] == second["event_id"]
+    assert len(store.get_stream()) == 1
+```
+
+```python
+def test_workspace_filter_and_pending_counts(tmp_path):
+    store = IntentStore(str(tmp_path / "e.db"))
+    store.append("JOB_CREATED", {"id": "a"}, workspace_id="ws-a")
+    store.append("JOB_CREATED", {"id": "b"}, workspace_id="ws-b")
+    assert [e["payload"]["id"] for e in store.get_stream(workspace_id="ws-a")] == ["a"]
+    assert store.pending_count("ws-a") == 1
+    store.mark_synced({store.get_stream(workspace_id="ws-a")[0]["event_id"]: 7})
+    assert store.pending_count("ws-a") == 0
+    assert store.get_cursor("ws-a") == 7
+```
+
+- [ ] **Step 2: Run tests to verify they fail**
+
+Run: `uv run pytest packages/core/tests/test_events.py packages/core/tests/test_intent_store.py -q`
+Expected: FAIL for missing fields/methods.
+
+- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the event contract and migration**
+
+Use `uuid.uuid4().hex` for `event_id`. Use `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()`
+for timestamps. Migration adds columns when absent:
+
+```sql
+ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN event_id TEXT;
+ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN workspace_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local';
+ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN device_id TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'local';
+ALTER TABLE events ADD COLUMN server_seq INTEGER;
+UPDATE events SET event_id = lower(hex(randomblob(16))) WHERE event_id IS NULL;
+CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_event_id ON events(event_id);
+CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_workspace_server ON events(workspace_id, server_seq);
+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sync_state (
+  workspace_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+  remote_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
+  last_server_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
+);
+```
+
+`get_stream(replay_order=True)` orders rows with `server_seq` first by
+`server_seq`, then pending rows by local `id`. `insert_remote` uses
+`INSERT OR IGNORE` and sets `server_seq`. `retag_workspace` updates rows and
+`sync_state`.
+
+- [ ] **Step 4: Run tests to verify they pass**
+
+Run: `uv run pytest packages/core/tests/test_events.py packages/core/tests/test_intent_store.py -q`
+Expected: PASS.
+
+- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**
+
+```bash
+git add packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/events.py packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/intent_store.py packages/core/tests/test_events.py packages/core/tests/test_intent_store.py
+git commit -m "feat(core): add sync-ready event store schema"
+```
+
+---
+
+### Task 2: Workspace-scoped repository and factory
+
+**Files:**
+- Modify: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/sqlite_repository.py`
+- Modify: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/factory.py`
+- Modify: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/__init__.py`
+- Test: `packages/core/tests/test_sqlite_repository.py`
+- Test: `packages/core/tests/test_repository_factory.py`
+
+**Interfaces:**
+- Produces: `EventSourcedRepository(db_path=None, workspace_id=None, store=None, device_id=None)`.
+- Keeps: `SQLiteRepository = EventSourcedRepository` compatibility alias.
+- Produces: `EventSourcedRepository.reload() -> None`.
+- Produces: `build_repository(db_path=None, workspace_id=None, device_id=None) -> Repository`.
+
+- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing tests**
+
+```python
+def test_repositories_are_workspace_isolated(tmp_path):
+    db = str(tmp_path / "odi.db")
+    a = EventSourcedRepository(db_path=db, workspace_id="ws-a")
+    b = EventSourcedRepository(db_path=db, workspace_id="ws-b")
+    a.add_job(Job(id="a", name="A"))
+    b.add_job(Job(id="b", name="B"))
+    assert [j.id for j in a.list_jobs()] == ["a"]
+    assert [j.id for j in b.list_jobs()] == ["b"]
+```
+
+```python
+def test_factory_reads_workspace_and_device(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_DB", str(tmp_path / "odi.db"))
+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_WORKSPACE", "ws-env")
+    repo = build_repository()
+    assert repo.workspace_id == "ws-env"
+```
+
+- [ ] **Step 2: Run tests to verify they fail**
+
+Run: `uv run pytest packages/core/tests/test_sqlite_repository.py packages/core/tests/test_repository_factory.py -q`
+Expected: FAIL for missing constructor arguments/behavior.
+
+- [ ] **Step 3: Implement workspace scoping**
+
+All `store.append` calls pass `workspace_id` and `device_id`. `_load_snapshot`
+uses `replay_order=True`. `reload()` calls `_load_snapshot()`. Add
+`workspace_id` and `device_id` attributes. Factory resolves env in this order:
+explicit argument, `AGENTIC_ODI_WORKSPACE`, `local`.
+
+- [ ] **Step 4: Run tests to verify they pass**

+# Local-First Storage with Optional Cloudflare D1 Sync Implementation Plan
+
+> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
+
+**Goal:** Add a sync-ready event store seam so local runs stay on SQLite, hosted runs use Cloudflare D1, and users can opt into authenticated sync or portable export/import.
+
+**Architecture:** `ODIService` is unchanged. `IntentStore` grows the sync fields and implements an `EventStore` protocol. `EventSourcedRepository` can sit over SQLite or D1. A new `agentic_odi_cloud` package provides the D1 REST provider, authenticated sync client, and JSONL bundles. A Worker owns D1 and Better Auth; local clients talk only to the sync API.
+
+**Tech Stack:** Python 3.10+, `httpx`, Cloudflare Workers, D1, Better Auth 1.5, TypeScript, Vitest, Miniflare.
+
+**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-storage-provider-sync-design.md`
+
+## Global Constraints
+
+- Python >= 3.10.
+- `packages/core` must continue to depend on no other workspace package.
+- Local mode must make zero data network calls.
+- `AGENTIC_ODI_STORAGE=local` always wins over D1 credentials.
+- Default local database remains `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`.
+- Tests run without Cloudflare credentials or network.
+- No secrets in source; `.dev.vars` is ignored.
+- Keep README/docs current in the same change.
+
+## Review Focus
+
+1. Malformed or hostile sync payloads must not corrupt local data or leak
+   another workspace's server sequence.
+2. Concurrent edits from two devices must converge to server order; deletes
+   must not be resurrected.
+3. Legacy databases must upgrade in place with unique event IDs and no loss.
+4. Local mode with D1 credentials present must still make no data network calls.
+5. Clock skew must not affect ordering; server sequence is authoritative.
+
+---
+

+

+- Modify: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/intent_store.py`

+- Test: `packages/core/tests/test_intent_store.py`

+  `new_event_id()`, `resolve_device_id(path: Path | None = None) -> str`.

# Local-First Storage with Optional Cloudflare D1 Sync

**Date:** 2026-10-20
**Status:** Approved for implementation

## Intent

The product promise is: open Agentic ODI and start working. There is no
database choice, no setup wizard, and no cloud requirement. Data lives on the
user's device by default. When the user wants another device or a teammate,
one action makes the work follow them.

The original request framed Cloudflare D1 as the default database with local
storage as a fallback. The final direction is the reverse: the environment
decides the store. A locally accessed app uses local SQLite. A hosted app uses
D1. A privacy-first user can force local mode even when cloud credentials are
present. D1 is the cloud adapter, not a tax on local users.

## Goals

- Keep zero-setup, offline, local-first behavior as the default.
- Make hosted deployments use Cloudflare D1 without duplicating ODI domain
  logic.
- Let a user opt into sync from a local database to the cloud.
- Support personal workspaces and Better Auth organizations (teams).
- Provide portable export/import as a trust and migration escape hatch.
- Make the enterprise self-hosted tier the same Worker + D1 deployment under
  the customer's own Cloudflare account.
- Keep the existing `ODIService` and MCP contract untouched.

## Non-Goals

- Studio sign-in, workspace switcher, and invitation UI in this slice.
- Hosted chat/LLM deployment and billing.
- Fine-grained field-level conflict resolution (CRDTs).
- Real-time push sync; v1 is explicit push/pull.
- Real Cloudflare deployment in CI.

## UX Principles

1. **No database question.** The user sees "on this device" or "synced", never
   "SQLite or D1".
2. **Local is not a fallback.** It is the privacy promise and the default for
   local access.
3. **Sync is an upgrade, not a migration project.** Signing in should carry
   existing local work along by re-tagging and uploading it, not by asking the
   user to export and re-import.
4. **One escape hatch.** `odi sync export` always produces a complete
   portable bundle; import is idempotent.
5. **Teams are workspaces.** A personal workspace is the user; a team is a
   Better Auth organization.

## Architecture

```text
Local plane (default, no auth, no network)
  SPA / CLI / MCP
    -> ODIService
    -> EventSourcedRepository
    -> IntentStore (SQLite)

Hosted plane (D1)
  Worker + Better Auth
    -> /api/sync/* (event push/pull)
    -> D1 events table
  Hosted sidecar (optional)
    -> D1EventStore (D1 REST API)
    -> ODIService

Bridge
  SyncService (local IntentStore <-> authenticated Worker)
```

The seam is the append-only event log, not the ORM. Local and cloud store the
same event rows. This keeps one domain implementation while allowing two
storage backends.

## Event Contract

Each event has:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Local insertion sequence (SQLite autoincrement) |
| `event_id` | Client-generated UUID, globally unique and idempotent |
| `workspace_id` | Tenant boundary; `local` for unlinked local data |
| `device_id` | Random per-device identifier, never a hostname |
| `timestamp` | ISO-8601 UTC observation time |
| `type` | Existing event types (`JOB_CREATED`, `OUTCOME_UPDATED`, ...) |
| `payload` | Existing JSON payload |
| `server_seq` | D1 `id` once the event has been pushed; `NULL` while pending |

The D1 `events.id` is the canonical server order. Timestamps are not used for
ordering, so clock skew cannot reorder work.

## Sync Protocol

- **Push:** local events with `server_seq IS NULL` are sent in local order. The
  server inserts with `INSERT OR IGNORE` on `event_id`, then returns the
  server sequence for each accepted event in the caller's workspace. Re-push is
  a no-op.
- **Pull:** the client asks for events after its cursor. The server returns
  events in `id` order. The client inserts them idempotently, records the
  cursor, and reloads its snapshot.
- **Conflict rule v1:** last write wins by `server_seq`. Updates are patch
  events; deletes are tombstones. A stale update cannot overwrite a newer
  server-ordered event after a pull reload. This is documented as a v1 limit.
- **Offline:** writes always succeed locally. Sync is explicit and can be
  retried safely.
- **Workspace link:** local data starts as `local`. On first sync the client may
  re-tag it to the authenticated personal or organization workspace. Export
  preserves workspace IDs.

## Storage Selection

`AGENTIC_ODI_STORAGE=auto|local|d1` (default `auto`).

- `auto`: use D1 only when all D1 credentials are present; otherwise SQLite.
- `local`: always SQLite, even when D1 credentials exist.
- `d1`: require D1 configuration and fail loudly if incomplete.

Local access never needs an account. Hosted deployments set `d1` explicitly.

## Auth and Tenancy

- Better Auth on D1 handles users, sessions, and organizations.
- Bearer auth is enabled for CLI/API clients; cookies support the future web UI.
- The authenticated workspace is the session's active organization, or the
  user's own ID for a personal workspace.
- Sync requests may only read/write the authenticated workspace. The Worker
  never trusts a client-supplied workspace beyond that comparison.
- Local mode has no auth and no identity.
- The D1 REST service token is server-side only; it is never given to clients.

## Self-Hosted Enterprise

The same Worker, D1 schema, and Python adapters deploy under a customer's
Cloudflare account. Configuration changes, not code forks:

- `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`
- D1 binding and database ID
- Optional identity provider (GitHub OAuth today, SSO later)
- Optional custom domain

## Security and Privacy

- Local mode performs no data network calls.
- Sync is opt-in per workspace.
- Batch limits: 500 events, 256 KiB per payload, 5 MiB per request.
- Event IDs, workspace IDs, device IDs, and event types are validated.
- SQL uses prepared statements.
- Cross-workspace event ID collisions are rejected without leaking the other
  workspace's sequence.
- Export bundles contain the user's data in clear JSONL; users control them.

## Failure Handling

- D1 unavailable: hosted reads/writes fail with a clear 5xx; local mode is
  unaffected. Sync retries are safe.
- Partial push: idempotent inserts mean the next push completes the batch.
- Legacy local DB: upgraded in place; event IDs are backfilled uniquely.
- Corrupt remote event: rejected without applying the rest of the batch.

## Verification

- Unit and integration tests must not require Cloudflare credentials.
- Worker tests use Miniflare with a local D1 database.
- The Python D1 client is tested with `httpx.MockTransport`.
- A local -> fake cloud -> fresh local round-trip proves the bridge.
- Full lint, typecheck, bandit, pytest, frontend, and Worker suites pass before
  the PR is opened.

parts.text:
The prior design is about Python CLI/server local-first with D1; different from browser BFF. But relevant.

Now let's think about scope and questions. We should determine:
1. Does the user want a *browser-local BFF* that makes the SPA fully functional without sidecar (CRUD/canvas, manual capture, scoring, job map, evidence?), or just a graceful fallback (read-only demo) with enhanced sidecar? The phrase "works without the sidecart" implies functional.
2. Should local data be authoritative/persistent, and should it sync/import to sidecar when it becomes available? Or should sidecar remain authoritative when present? The CTO guidance strongly pushes local-first source of truth with sync overlay. But implementing sync now may be too much. Need to clarify.
3. Storage tech: OPFS SQLite WASM vs IndexedDB. CTO explicitly recommends SQLite OPFS. But to keep this repo's tests/deploy simple, IndexedDB is safer. We should present tradeoff and recommend one. Maybe use `@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm` worker with OPFS; CSP needs `worker-src`, `wasm-unsafe-eval`, and COOP/COEP? Let's research quickly? Actually I know sqlite-wasm OPFS VFS in Chrome requires COOP/COEP for SharedArrayBuffer? The official sqlite3 WASM OPFS VFS uses `Atomics.wait` and requires cross-origin isolation in some builds? Let me verify. The `@sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm` "opfs" VFS requires COOP/COEP headers for SharedArrayBuffer, I believe. There's also "opfs-sahpool" which doesn't need SharedArrayBuffer but is single-connection and uses sync access handles; Chrome 108+, Safari 16.4+, Firefox 111+. Using `opfs-sahpool` may avoid COOP/COEP. Cloudflare Worker security headers currently set `default-src 'self'`; would need `worker-src 'self' blob:` perhaps, and `script-src 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` (WASM compile) or `'unsafe-eval'`. Adding COOP/COEP can break cross-origin resources. This is a real consideration.

Also Tauri: desktop uses native sidecar? Docs say Tauri shell. If browser BFF uses OPFS, Tauri webview OPFS support differs (WebView2/WebKit). CTO says native SQLite in Tauri, but current Tauri shell likely just wraps SPA and talks to sidecar. We could keep desktop sidecar path.

Alternative local storage: IndexedDB via `idb` library. Simpler, broadly supported, no CSP changes, works in Tauri webview. Persistence is less "SQLite parity" but for the domain (few entities) it's fine. The CTO guidance is inspiration, not strict mandate. But the user may expect SQLite.

4. Capability disclosure UX: badge/panel? Should features be hidden, disabled with explanation, or upsell? "graceful progressive capability disclosure" implies show available local capabilities, and advertise enhanced sidecar capabilities with a clear "Connect sidecar" path. Need design.

5. Should the Worker advertise capabilities? Currently `/api/config` probe determines sidecar reachability. Could add `/api/capabilities` richer manifest. Worker can return capabilities even when no sidecar (local-only), e.g., a static endpoint. But the SPA's local BFF can self-report capabilities. Enhanced capability detection should be explicit and reliable: e.g., `GET /api/capabilities` returns `{deployment, features: {chat: bool, connectors: bool, memory: bool, mcp: bool, conversationHistory: bool}, storage}`. When no sidecar, Worker should respond 200 with capabilities local-only, not 502. But `run_worker_first` intercepts /api; we can add a Worker route for /api/capabilities that returns local capabilities, and only proxy other /api. Or BFF in SPA simply probes /api/config; but that 502s. Better to have the Worker implement a "capability manifest" endpoint and return it. But local dev (Vite) has no Worker. The SPA can default to local BFF and probe sidecar availability.

6. Chat without sidecar: Could call LLM directly from browser if user configures an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that allows CORS. But currently the sidecar hides key and proxies. For Tier 0, chat could be unavailable; manual mode. The user says "enhanced capabilities with [sidecar]" — chat is likely the main enhancement. But maybe they want basic offline deterministic assistant (existing offline fallback) locally. The chat endpoint itself requires sidecar. After BFF, a local "chat" could return the deterministic offline fallback, but that's already the sidecar's behavior without LLM. Could we move the offline fallback into the client? That would allow a "conversation" without sidecar, but no tool loop. Might be nice but scope creep.

Also there are features like "catch up", "notifications", "changelog", "health". `fetchChangelog` from C H A N G E L O G file (sidecar). Could bundle locally. `fetchConfig` defaults. Could be local constants.

7. Data migration/persistence: If a user has local BFF data and then connects sidecar, should we push local data to sidecar (via API) or pull sidecar data? The CTO guidance says local is source of truth and sync overlay. But current sidecar is authoritative. A pragmatic v1: local data is persisted and used in local mode; when sidecar is available, sidecar becomes the source for the session (with local data offered as import or hidden). But that violates local-first continuity. Better: on sidecar connect, offer "Bring this device's work into the sidecar" (one-way import) or "Use sidecar workspace" (leave local). Or merge with IDs. Need to decide.

Perhaps the best plan is to introduce a `StudioBackend` interface with two implementations and a coordinator. The coordinator detects capabilities and selects:
- Local BFF is always the read/write source for ODI artifacts (canvas + CRUD) to guarantee offline.
- Sidecar, when present, is used for enhanced capabilities (chat, connectors, MCP, memory) AND as an optional replication target for artifacts. But then chat tools modify sidecar data, while local BFF is separate -> divergence. Could have chat tool calls route through sidecar and then refresh local? Complex. Alternatively, when sidecar present, use sidecar as the source (current behavior), and local BFF only when absent. That's simplest, but data doesn't follow. User may accept.

The task: "back-of-the-front-end type of implementation that supports graceful progressive capability disclosure in that it works without the sidecart, but gets access to enhanced capabilities with it." This sounds like a facade/aggregator, not a full sync engine. The BFF picks providers per capability. The local provider covers core data offline; the remote provider covers enhanced features. "Progressive capability disclosure" = detect and reveal.

Given CTO guidance, we should frame local-first but constrain scope: local BFF is the source of truth for ODI artifacts in the browser; when sidecar is connected, we offer explicit handoff/import/export rather than silent dual-write. Or implement one-way import on first connect and then sidecar authoritative? Hmm.

Let's inspect if current sidecar API has bulk import/export endpoints. Search router: no import. CLI perhaps has export? Search.

# Running The Living Studio

**The Living Studio** is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation:
an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact
Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent
connected to the MCP server.

The Studio runs three ways locally, plus a hosted deployment. All of them serve
the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:8100` — the
SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly.

## Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
│  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)    │
│  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
│  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
└────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                             │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                             │  - conversations + PM memory  │
                                             └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                             │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                             ▼
                                             ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                             │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                             ▲
                                                             │ OpenAI-compatible
                                             ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                             │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
```

## Interface

The Studio opens as a conversation, not a dashboard.

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| **First-run tour** | A four-step, skippable welcome on the very first visit: what the studio is, which ambition brought you here, the live state of your sidecar/MCP/model (with inline repair when the model is down), and the first move. The four doors are **I have one in mind**, **My boss handed me a priority**, **Help me find the next one**, and **Pressure-test a bet**; each starts the matching conversation. Replay it from **Settings → Replay the welcome tour**. |
| **First run** | A short conversation in the chat, not a form: what you are building, who feels the problem, the job they are trying to get done, then where it hurts. One question at a time, with a reflection before the next ask, quick replies, and **Explore on my own** always visible. Skipping is allowed; answers and progress are kept as a draft. Re-open it any time with `/start`, the home stage's context pill, or Settings. |
| **Hero** | One rotating headline above the composer: a greeting (time of day, plus your name if you set one in Settings), the product/job you set up, what is already on the canvas, or an intent-first prompt such as *What are you trying to win this quarter?* It cycles every few seconds and stays still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. |
| **Suggestion pills** | Below the headline. **Sharpen an opportunity** always starts a conversation; the next pill becomes **Pressure-test a bet** once outcomes exist, or **Find the next opportunity** before that. **Capture what you heard** replaces the landscape pill once a job exists. They change as the canvas fills up. |
| **Composer** | Docked at the bottom of the transcript. `Enter` sends, `Shift`+`Enter` adds a line, `Cmd/Ctrl`+`K` focuses it, and `/` opens the command palette. The send button becomes a stop button while a reply streams. |
| **Bar** | The only persistent chrome: home, new conversation, catch-up, live model status, and settings. There is no navigation drawer to compete with the thread. |
| **Rail** | Above the conversation, and only once the thread has produced something: `Landscape · N`, `Job map · N`, `Evidence · N`, `What I know · N`. Every item is derived from the canvas and the memory, so the strip is a record of the work rather than a fixed menu. |
| **Lens** | A view docks to the right of the thread on wide screens and becomes a full-height sheet on narrow ones. The transcript and the composer stay on screen and stay usable; `Esc`, **Close**, or the rail chip closes it. Every lens ends in one sentence that re-enters the conversation — *Ask which to chase*, *Walk me through the job*, *Weigh the evidence* — so leaving a view is never a return to a menu. Settings and catch-up use the same lens. |

Replies render Markdown (headings, lists, emphasis, inline and fenced code).
Tool calls appear inline as small trace chips while the agent works.

### Slash commands

Type `/` to open the palette. `Up`/`Down` move, `Enter` or `Tab` runs the
selected command, `Esc` closes it. Commands are handled in the SPA and never call
the model, so they work when it is offline.

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/help` | Every command, as a notice in the transcript |
| `/start` | Resume the context conversation |
| `/new` | New conversation |
| `/home` | Return to the empty stage |
| `/jobs` | Job summary, then the job map |
| `/landscape`, `/jobmap`, `/evidence`, `/settings` | Open that lens beside the conversation |
| `/impact`, `/capture` | Start the conversation that produces the card. `/capture` falls back to the offline form when no model answers. |
| `/status` | Model, MCP, context, and canvas status |

Unknown commands produce a transcript notice pointing at `/help`.

### The welcome tour

The tour is the front door, the context conversation is the first room. It is
skippable at every step (`Skip the tour` or `Escape`), resumable (progress is
stored after every transition in `localStorage["studio.onboarding"]`), and
replayable from Settings.

Everything lives in `apps/studio/src/onboarding/`:

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `content.ts` | Steps and goal copy as typed data — the only place the words live |
| `machine.ts` | Pure state transitions, no React or storage |
| `storage.ts` | Versioned, defensive `localStorage` persistence |
| `OnboardingProvider.tsx` | Auto-open, persistence, replay |
| `FirstRunWizard.tsx`, `steps.tsx`, `onboarding.css` | The dialog |
| `../features/flags.ts` | The `firstRunWizard` toggle |

`App.tsx` only wires the provider and the wizard around the existing shell;
the chat, canvas, and sidecar code are untouched.

#### Toggling the tour

`firstRunWizard` defaults to on. Resolution order, highest first:

| Source | Example | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Query parameter | `?flags=firstRunWizard:off` | QA a build without rebuilding |
| Local override | `localStorage["studio.flags.firstRunWizard"] = "off"` | Per-browser opt-out |
| Build environment | `VITE_STUDIO_FIRST_RUN_WIZARD=off npm --prefix apps/studio run build` | Ship it dark |
| Default | on | |

Accepted values are `1`/`0`, `true`/`false`, `on`/`off`, `yes`/`no`, and
`enabled`/`disabled`. With the flag off, no dialog renders, no onboarding state
is written, and Settings hides the replay action.

### Guidance, not gates

The setup conversation is a nudge, never a prerequisite. If you skip it, the
home stage keeps a dashed **Tell me what you're building** pill; it reopens the
conversation exactly where you left off. `/start` and Settings do the same. The conversation also understands a
natural reply: say "skip", "not now", or "show me the landscape" and it reacts
instead of recording it as an answer. When a brief exists, it opens on a review
and asks what changed rather than asking everything again.

### Without a model

When the LLM is unreachable the Studio keeps working:

- A **Working by hand** strip explains the state and offers capture, job map,
  and context.
- Messages still return deterministic ODI guidance from the sidecar, labelled
  **Local guidance**.
- Jobs can be created, renamed, and deleted; steps added, edited, and removed;
  outcomes recorded, re-scored, and removed. All of it goes through the same
  local repository the model uses.
- Settings → Base URL and Model reconnect the assistant whenever you are ready.

The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from
the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.

### The thread is the room

Capture, scoring, simulation, and decisions are conversations. The storefront
never asks the PM to leave the thread to do work: the agent asks for the
customer's words or the bet in plain language, then renders the surface that
carries it. A lens exists for reading and for people who prefer a click, not for
doing the work.

                    "role": "assistant",
                    "content": "".join(turn_text) or None,
                    "tool_calls": [
                        {
                            "id": entry["id"],
                            "type": "function",
                            "function": {
                                "name": entry["name"],
                                "arguments": entry["arguments"] or "{}",
                            },
                        }
                        for entry in tool_calls.values()
                    ],
                }
            )

            for entry in tool_calls.values():
                name = entry["name"]
                arguments = _parse_arguments(entry["arguments"])
                counters["tool_calls"] += 1

                if name == "add_connector":
                    result_str, events = _apply_add_connector(arguments, connector_service)
                    for event in events:
                        yield frame(event["event"], event["data"])
                elif name == "remember":

                    result_str, memory_event = _apply_remember(arguments, memory)

                        counters["tool_errors"] += 1
                        yield frame(

                    else:
                        yield frame("tool", {"name": name, "status": "ok"})

                else:

                            )
                            counters["tool_errors"] += 1

        )

        yield frame("message", {"content": content})

async def stream_chat(
    request: ChatRequest,
    service: ConnectorService | None = None,
    memory: StudioMemory | None = None,
    request_id: str | None = None,
) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
    """Yield SSE frames: status, conversation, delta, tool, ui, memory, connector, message, error.

    Every turn ends with exactly one terminal event: one ``message`` or one
    ``error``. A failure is never dressed up as a success, and it never leaves
    the stream without an ending.
    """
    rid = request_id or ""
    started = time.monotonic()
    counters = {"rounds": 0, "tool_calls": 0, "tool_errors": 0, "rounds_exhausted": 0}
    outcome = "failed"
    error_code: str | None = None
    try:
        async for chunk in _turn_frames(request, service, memory, rid, counters):
            yield chunk
        outcome = "completed"
        if counters["tool_errors"]:
            outcome = "partial"
        if counters["rounds_exhausted"]:
            outcome = "rounds_exhausted"
    except _TurnFailure as failure:
        yield _error_frame(failure.error, rid)
        outcome = "failed"
        error_code = failure.error.code.value
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
        log.exception("chat turn failed (request_id=%s)", rid)
        yield _error_frame(
            StudioError(
                code=StudioErrorCode.INTERNAL,
                message="The turn failed unexpectedly.",
                suggestion="Try again — your question is still here.",
            ),
            rid,
        )
        outcome = "failed"
    finally:
        log_turn(
            request_id=rid,
            model=request.model,
            rounds=counters["rounds"],
            tool_calls=counters["tool_calls"],
            tool_errors=counters["tool_errors"],
            duration_ms=int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),
            outcome=outcome,
            error_code=error_code,
        )


__all__ = [
    "REMEMBER_TOOL",
    "SYSTEM_PROMPT",
    "offline_fallback",
    "stream_chat",
]
